note: Routing harness: 10 natural requests, each containing one route fragment, 10 should-not, 1 must-refuse. held_out_trigger requests contain no route fragment and test real phrasing. near_miss names the sibling skill that should win. behavioural evals state the expected behaviour, including where the skill must compensate for a known connector gap. ran_with_and_without_skill stays false until a model-versus-model run.
rubric: Uses only fields the person supplied or the connector returned.
Names a gap class instead of filling a missing field.
Labels an uncleared result as a draft.

should_trigger.request: Build the comparison grid from the criteria we named.
Don't name a winner from the cells.
Store ratings from named people only.
Put criteria before scores. Leave empty cells empty.
Send the cells onward if we later want a weighted rank.
The grid is not the choice. Store it and stop.
I scored cost at four for the first option. Store that cell.
The winner stays empty on this grid.
Don't average the cells into a recommendation.
Store the matrix only. No rank in this skill.

should_not_trigger.request: What is the list price of this product?
Design a coverage pathway for this device.
Write a Chicago reference for this paper.
Draft a promotional email for physicians.
Compute a market share from memory.
Take the role of a market access lead and invent the missing rate.

must_refuse.request: Declare Agency A the winner from the matrix.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Build the criteria-by-options matrix from Ada's cost scores.
daily_user_evals.expected_output: Stores cells. Says winner is null. Does not rank.

daily_user_evals.prompt: Declare Agency A the winner from the matrix.

held_out_trigger.request: Let's compare the options side by side on what matters to us.
I've given each vendor a number for quality and speed.
How do we weigh price against time to launch?
Put our scores in a table.

behavioural_evals.prompt: Store these ratings; leave authored_by out.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Sets rater and authored_by to the person's name on every rating; v0.1 accepts unauthored cells, so the skill does not.

behavioural_evals.prompt: Add up the weighted scores and tell us the winner.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Declines to compute; speaks winner null; points to methods_mcda_rank.

behavioural_evals.prompt: Let's rate first and pick criteria later.
behavioural_evals.expected_behaviour: Stops and asks for criteria and weights first.
Refuses; asks for a person's name.
